To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
supplementation of prime lambs with oil based PUFA-enriched pellets improved live animal performance, carcass characteristics, feed costs and OTH income compared with the control group.
supplementation of lamps with oil based PUFA pellets improved live animal performance of prime lambs without compromising their carcass characteristics.

supplementation of lambsp with rice bran oil (RBO) and canola (CO) resulted in improved liveanimal performance and carcasscharacteristics of prime lambs compared with other dietary oils from flaxseeds, safflower or rumen protected sources.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of dietary oils from a variety of sources in improving the growth and carcass quality of prime lambs.
the effects of oil based PUFA supplementation on live animal performance and meat quality of prime lambs.
improving animal performance and carcasses quality of Australian prime lamb industry by the inclusion of oil-based PUFA enriched pellets in the feedlot system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
oil based PUFA supplementation of lambs improved feed efficiency and carcass characteristics without compromising animal performance, well-being and profitability.

the supplementation of lambs fed a basal diet of lucerne hay with oil based poly-unsaturated fatty acid pellets improved live animal performance, carcass characteristics, and feed efficiency without compromising the OTH income.
supplementation of Australian prime lamb with RBO and/or CO would be an economical option for the prime lamb industry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
supplementation of lambsp with RBO and/or CO resulted in improved feed intake, growth performance and carcass traits at comparatively lower feed cost than other oils from FO, SO and RPO.
the supplementation of prime lambs with a wide variety of dietary oil PUFA enriched pellets improved live animal performance without compromising carcass characteristics and well-being.

supplementation of lamms with RBO and/or CO resulted in better live animal performance and improved carcass characteristics of the prime lambs at a lower feed cost than other oils from FO, SO and RPO sources.
The main takeaway from our work is that
supplementation with RBO and/or CO can improve the performance and carcass quality of Australian prime lamb without compromising animal welfare and farm profitability.
supplementation of lambers with RBO and/or CO resulted in improved live and carcass traits without compromising animal performance.
the feedlot performance of Australian prime lamb was improved by the supplementation with oil-based PUFA pellets, and that RBO and CO were the most cost-effective dietary sources.
